name: goose Code Mode (code_execution platform extension)
engine: Boa 0.22.0 (pure-Rust JS interpreter) on a dedicated OS thread inside the goose process; no OS sandbox
how_run: Rust harness compiles goose's javascript.rs verbatim (include!) and calls javascript::execute, the function CodeExecutionClient::handle_execute_javascript calls (code_execution.rs:123), with goose's 300 s default timeout and a lookup callback dispatched onto the host runtime like dispatch_tool; the MCP/agent layer above it was not built.

defaults.time: 300 s wall deadline (goose DEFAULT_EXTENSION_TIMEOUT, overridable by GOOSE_DEFAULT_EXTENSION_TIMEOUT); plus Boa limits of 2,000,000 VM instructions, 100,000 loop iterations per frame, recursion 128. Native builtins (regex) are not counted, and the deadline cannot stop the worker thread.
defaults.memory: none (P7b, P7c reached 4 GB in under 0.4 s)
defaults.output: 1,000,000 bytes for console output plus serialized return value combined; exceeding it is an error, not a truncation
defaults.tool_calls: no count limit; at most 4 concurrent executions process-wide (WORKER_SLOTS)

source_notes.finding: No generated interface. One native object `tools` with a single method `call(name, args)`; args must be a JSON object. Model writes `async function run()`; goose appends `;run();`.
On demand. The model sees three tools: list_functions (name + first line of description, 240 chars), get_function_details (original JSON input/output schemas), execute_javascript.

Boa NativeFunction::from_async_fn; the async job is polled by goose's own job loop on the worker thread; the callback spawns the MCP call onto goose's main tokio runtime. Tool results are flattened to assistant-visible text and JSON-parsed if possible.

Boa interpreter in-process, on a thread named goose-javascript. Claimed boundary (INSTRUCTIONS): 'isolated, with no filesystem, shell, network, packages, or environment access'. Code matches for capabilities (no host objects, IdleModuleLoader, timers rejected) but there is no memory cap and native builtins escape the CPU limits.
Captured console lines plus 'Result: <JSON of run() return>' in one text block. 1,000,000-byte combined limit raises an error. Errors are prefixed 'Error: ' and capped by limit_error.

INSTRUCTION_LIMIT 2,000,000; loop limit 100,000; recursion 128; WORKER_SLOTS 4; timeout from goose config (default 300 s). Boa charges String.prototype.repeat per iteration against the loop limit, which is why the spec's repeat() probes fail.
Fresh Boa Context per execute_javascript call; no snapshot, no persistence API.
Boa JsError to_string includes message, location and stack; syntax errors get a hint to define async function run().

Code mode is behind cargo feature `code-mode` (on in goose-cli default features) and the extension is default_enabled: false. Tool calls from JS reuse goose's normal tool dispatch (CallRequest), so approvals and permissions of the underlying tools apply; summon's delegate and app-only/resource tools are excluded from the catalog.

surprises: The Dec 2025 blog says goose 'generates a JavaScript interface representing the connected MCP tools'. At this commit there is no generated interface: one tools.call(name, args) proxy plus list_functions/get_function_details discovery (code_execution.rs:25).
Boa's 100,000 loop limit is charged per String.prototype.repeat iteration, so ordinary code like "A".repeat(200000) fails with RuntimeLimitError (P2, P7).
No memory limit: 4 GB in 0.3 s, inside the goose agent process itself (P7b, P7c).

CPU limits count VM instructions only. A catastrophic regex ran past 120 s (P6b); after goose's 300 s deadline the thread keeps running and holds one of only 4 process-wide worker slots (javascript.rs:28,384-386,409-423).
Error headline location points at goose's appended ';run();' line (code_mode.js:4:5), not the throw; the stack frame below it is correct (P10).
The blog links block/goose; the repo now lives at aaif-goose/goose.
